_what: C-9: HER CAST-START HITCH (the coordinator, from lane B's control runs: a frame of 33.8 ms on desktop, 22.9 on the web, about 140 ms after the cast input, with no effect in the scene) -- found, fixed, measured. godot/tools/perf_cast.gd --c sorceress --no-fx: the painted Barrow in the root viewport, desktop Forward+ 1920x1080 on the M2, vsync off; 12 control casts (slash, chop alternately, 3 s apart, by try_strike); every frame split by the engine's own signals into physics / process / draw

cause.1_trail_upload: her strike STEPS, and a step into the snow stamps a print: SnowField._stamp marks the trail map dirty and _process re-sent the WHOLE map -- 1024^2 RGBAF, 16 MB -- through ImageTexture.update(_gpu_image(...)): 14-17 ms of process (PackedFloat32Array.to_byte_array + Image.create_from_data, two 16 MB copies) and then the upload inside the next draw (21-51 ms). The frame lands where her feet land: about +130 ms into the Fire Ball, +310-340 ms into the Meteor. Not every cast: only when a foot has travelled stamp_stride_m (0.19 m) since its last print.
cause.2_puff_realloc: the same print kicks a snow puff, and SnowField._puff SET GPUParticles3D.amount per print (13 x depth factor, or the spray's 46): a new amount re-allocates the particle buffers on that frame. With the trail upload switched off (--no-trail-upload, a diagnosis switch) this alone still spiked the draw to 19.7-25.6 ms at the same moments.
cause.not: not her clip starting, not the tree's clip switch (her physics step, the AnimationTree included, stayed 0.2-0.7 ms on every spike frame; the tree cleared no caches), not spell_fx (off in these runs), no pipeline compiles (RenderingServer's counters did not move after the first frame)
cause.who_else: him too: his steps stamp the same map, so every print he left -- walking included -- paid the same 16 MB upload

fix.trail: snow_field.gd: the trail map is a Texture2DArray of 128^2 tiles, each with a one-texel APRON (its neighbours' edge texels; the map's own edge texel, clamped, at the border); a print marks only the tiles it touched (and the neighbours whose apron holds its edge texels), and _process re-sends only those: 130^2 x 16 B = 270 KB a tile (desktop RGBAF; 135 KB RGBAH on the web). SnowField.SHADER's trail_at() and the heather's _press() pick the tile and sample inside the apron. PROBE (godot/tools/probe_trail_tiles.gd): random trail values, the old single texture and the new tiles sampled at 640,000 sub-texel positions across every tile border and both map edges: max |old - new| = 0.000000 on Forward+ (1024, RGBAF); 0.000244 on Compatibility (512, RGBAH: one half-float rounding step, mean 1e-8).
fix.puffs: snow_field.gd: the puff pool is sized once at the most any print can ask for (max(spray 46, 13 x 4.0) = 52) and a print sets GPUParticles3D.amount_ratio (want / 52) instead of amount: no re-allocation.
